data.gender_notes: Gwyneth is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Gwyneth comes from the Welsh word ‘gwyn’, which means ‘fair’, ‘white’, or ‘blessed’. In Welsh mythology, Gwyneth was a goddess of the moon, fertility, and women. The name Gwyneth carries the meaning “Fair, white, blessed” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gwyneth usually hope their child will grow to embody fair, white, blessed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Gwyneth belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair, white, blessed.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gwyneth total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: גוונת
in_hebrew.meaning: גוונת משמע הלבן או השמחה או הברכה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: גוונת הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשפה הוולשית, אך ניתן לראות את הקשר שלו למילה העברית 'גוון' שמשמעותה צבע או גוון, וייתכן שיש קשר רוחני למושג הברכה או השמחה המוזכרים בתנ'ך, כמו בשיר השירים 4:3 'ואמרו בעמק גוונך'.

in_greek.name: Γουίνεθ
in_greek.meaning: Γουίνεθ σημαίνει λευκός ή χαρά ή ευλογία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Γουίνεθ είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την Ουαλία, αλλά μπορεί να συνδεθεί με την ελληνική λέξη 'γουν', που σημαίνει χρώμα ή απόχρωση, και πιθανώς έχει πνευματική σχέση με την έννοια της ευλογίας ή της χαράς που αναφέρονται στη Βίβλο, όπως στο Ψαλμό 16:11 'και πληρώσεις με ευλογία'.

data.cultural_impact: Gwyneth was a popular given name in Wales and England during the Middle Ages. It was borne by several saints and is mentioned in various literary works. Over the centuries, the name fell out of favor, but it was revived in the late 20th century due to the popularity of the actress Gwyneth Paltrow. Today, the name is once again gaining popularity, particularly in the English-speaking world, as a unique and beautiful name for a baby girl.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gwyneth carries a deep spiritual meaning, signifying purity, brightness, and blessings. It is a reminder of the divine feminine energy that nurtures and sustains life. For Christians, it can be seen as a reflection of the virtues of purity, humility, and grace embodied by the Blessed Virgin Mary. It is also a reminder of the spiritual struggle to maintain a pure heart and a clear mind in the face of life's challenges, striving to live a life pleasing to God and reflecting His divine light to the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gwyneth, meaning "white, fair, holy one," embodies the radiant purity and divine grace of the Christian faith. It is a gentle reminder of the inner light that shines within each believer, guiding them through life's journey towards the love and wisdom of God.

historical_references.reference: Gwyneth, daughter of Caradog ap Iestyn, was a Welsh princess who married King Seisyllog Ogam of Dumnonia in the late 5th or early 6th century.

historical_references.reference: Gwyneth, also known as Saint Winifred, was a 7th century Welsh saint whose story tells of her miraculous recovery from a mortal wound inflicted by a local priest who desired her.
